description: Figure 1 is a grouped bar chart comparing the performance and token efficiency of four reasoning methods—CoT, CoD, CCoT, and CoUT—across four large reasoning models (LRMs) evaluated on four benchmarks. The chart features two y-axes: the left axis, labeled “Accuracy (%)”, ranges from 70 to 100 in increments of 5, and the right axis, labeled “Token Count”, ranges from 0 to 800 in increments of 100. Each method is represented by a distinct color: red for CoT, orange for CoD, light blue for CCoT, and green for CoUT. For each method, two bars are shown: the left bar indicates accuracy (left y-axis) and the right bar indicates token count (right y-axis). Specifically, CoT achieves 91.19% accuracy with 676.85 tokens; CoD achieves 80.89% accuracy with 534.24 tokens; CCoT achieves 88.50% accuracy with 445.91 tokens; and CoUT achieves 88.40% accuracy with 354.46 tokens. The chart visually demonstrates that CoUT achieves comparable accuracy to CCoT while using significantly fewer tokens, and substantially fewer tokens than CoT, which has the highest accuracy but also the highest token count. The caption below the chart reads: “Figure 1: Average Performance and Tokens of CoUT and Baselines for 4 LRMs over 4 Benchmarks.”
